page_title: One wallpaper across multiple monitors in macOS | SpreadPaper

summary.name: SpreadPaper
summary.one_liner: A free, open source, native macOS app that stretches one wallpaper across multiple monitors, lining it up across the bezels.
use_cases: Spreading one panoramic photo across two or three monitors
Switching wallpaper between light and dark appearance automatically
Running a wallpaper that changes through the day on a schedule
Lining up a picture across monitor bezels of different sizes
Keeping a single still wallpaper stretched over a multi-display setup
summary.what_it_does: SpreadPaper takes one photograph and lays it across all connected displays, arranged on a canvas that mirrors the real monitor layout. It can compensate for bezels by offsetting displays by the bezel width so the image continues across the gap. It supports three kinds of wallpaper: a static single image, a Light and Dark pair that follows macOS appearance, and a dynamic HEIC desktop of up to 16 images on a time schedule. Each display gets its own rendered file keyed on display ID, and a gallery stores presets that can be renamed, duplicated, or deleted.
notable: Bezel compensation that offsets displays by bezel width so the picture lines up across monitors
Dynamic HEIC desktop with up to 16 timed images
Each display rendered separately by display ID, so identical monitors do not share a file
MIT licensed, source on GitHub with releases built by GitHub Actions
caveats: Requires macOS 15 Sequoia or later; Intel or Apple silicon Macs supported, but older macOS is not
Not signed with a paid Apple Developer ID, so macOS shows an unverified-malware warning and needs a manual bypass on first launch
Spanning a single photo across displays needs two or more monitors; Light/Dark and scheduled modes work on one screen
